title: Cipher and Cover
premise: Rafael Halloran, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Liaison Office—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a meeting request from his handler, sent hours after the man's autopsy. The invitation lures him into a live operation: extracting Dr. Ilse Varga, a cryptographer who defected with proof that the Office's director has been selling identities to hostile services. Rafael realizes Varga may be bait in a trap to flush out everyone who knows the director's secret, and that his own fabricated identity is the next thing to be sold. Racing a border checkpoint shift change, he chooses to burn the Office itself, exposing the director and trading his own cover for Varga's survival.
about_author: Casper Yarrow is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade working contracts near diplomatic compounds before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs officially never happened.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A routine document-burn job ends with Rafael finding a meeting invite from handler Anton Brek, timestamped after Brek's autopsy. The emotional beat is cold unease—Rafael has survived by trusting procedure, and procedure just spoke from the grave. He decides to attend, telling himself it's containment, not curiosity.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, flashback-woven. At the meeting site—a shuttered consular annex—he finds evidence someone used his credentials to book it. Interstitial scenes establish the Office: Director Cassian Voss, unlisted floors, identities issued like currency. The beat is dread of institutional power; Rafael realizes he was invited as Rafael Halloran, a name only three people alive should know.

chapters.title: Cargo Named Varga
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Varga. The defector waits in a safehouse, decoding files she stole proving Voss sold covers to a rival service. She doesn't trust her extraction team; she recognizes one escort's face from a file marked SOLD. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve—she copies everything twice, hiding one set where only a desperate fixer would look.

chapters.title: Shift Change at Kilometer Nine
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Recon of the border checkpoint reveals the shift rotation window: eleven minutes when both watchlists are offline. His contact inside warns him the checkpoint's new software came from a vendor tied to Voss. Beat: the trap takes shape—the escape route itself is the kill box, and Rafael must decide whether Varga is cargo or bait.

chapters.title: What the Handler Knew
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, dual timeline with Brek's final week. Digging through Brek's effects, Rafael finds the dead handler had been running a private audit of Voss—and had chosen Rafael as his insurance. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose; Rafael stops asking who killed Brek and starts asking what Brek wanted finished.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: POV Voss. The director reviews a ledger of purchased identities—Rafael's among them, marked for transfer at week's end. Voss is not a cartoon villain but a true believer protecting the Office by monetizing its secrets. Beat: chilling banality of corruption; readers see Rafael's death scheduled like freight.

chapters.title: Two Copies
chapters.summary: POV Rafael and Varga converging. Rafael finds the hidden duplicate of Varga's files, confirming her story and Voss's guilt—but also confirming she was tracked the moment she hid them. They meet hostile, negotiate wary alliance. Beat: two survivors recognizing each other's price tags; trust built from mutual exposure.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rafael/Varga. The extraction run begins: decoy convoy, forged manifests, the checkpoint approach timed to the shift gap. Everything breaks early—a sold identity flags their vehicle. Beat: rising panic into cold competence; Rafael improvises using the very corruption he's fighting, trading a burned alias for passage.

chapters.title: Cover Story
chapters.summary: Climax. POV Rafael. Cornered between Voss's cleaners and the border, Rafael broadcasts Varga's archive to every service the Office ever betrayed—including his own handlers' ghosts. Voss confronts him personally; the confrontation is verbal first, lethal second. Beat: cathartic sacrifice—Rafael destroys his own legend to make the truth undeniable.

chapters.title: No Attribution
chapters.summary: Resolution. POV Varga, then Rafael. Varga testifies under a name that never existed; Voss falls quietly, the Office rebranded rather than destroyed—power survives, diminished. Rafael, officially deceased, walks through a train station as no one at all. Beat: bittersweet freedom—he paid the full price of survival and finds it almost enough.
